data.long_meaning: In the Bible, Zacchaeus was a short man who climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus when He passed by. Jesus recognized Zacchaeus and praised him for his faith. The name Zaccheus carries the meaning “Small or little” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zaccheus usually hope their child will grow to embody small or little and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Zaccheus was a chief tax collector and a wealthy man in the city of Jericho. When Jesus passed through the city, Zaccheus, who was a short man, wanted to see him but couldn't because of the crowd. He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore-fig tree to get a better view of Jesus. Jesus called out to him and told him to come down, for he wanted to stay at Zaccheus's house. Zaccheus was overjoyed and immediately pledged to give half his wealth to the poor and to make things right with anyone he had cheated.
historical_references.context: New Testament of the Bible, Luke 19:1-10

historical_references.reference: The name Zaccheus is believed to be derived from the Hebrew name 'Zakkai', meaning 'pure'. It is also speculated that the name could have originated from the Aramaic word 'zikka', meaning 'short'. The name is most famously associated with the biblical character of the same name, who was a tax collector in the time of Jesus.
historical_references.time_period: Unknown, likely before the 1st century AD

In modern contexts, he is often used as a symbol of determination and ingenuity. In Christian media, Zaccheus' story is told as a reminder of God's ability to save anyone, regardless of their past sins. On social media, his name is used as a hashtag (#Zaccheus) to represent overcoming obstacles and persevering against all odds. In the business world, Zaccheus is referred to as a 'Red Hat Entrepreneur,' emphasizing his entrepreneurial spirit and his ability to succeed despite his physical limitations. This modern usage of the name Zaccheus reflects the enduring appeal of the biblical story and its relevance to contemporary issues of perseverance and success.
